name: Forth Bridge
hint: Three giant double cantilevers balance out from their piers, with short suspended spans between them.

history.name: Forth Bridge
history.location: Firth of Forth, near Edinburgh, Scotland
history.engineer: Sir John Fowler and Sir Benjamin Baker (contractor Sir William Arrol)
history.span: Two main spans of 521 m (1,700 ft)
facts: After the Tay Bridge collapsed in a gale in 1879, the Forth Bridge was designed for a wind pressure of 56 lb per square foot.
To explain how it works, engineer Kaichi Watanabe sat on a chair slung between Fowler and Baker, whose arms and sticks were the cantilevers - the famous "human cantilever".
It holds about 6.5 million rivets and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015.
history.why: When it opened it had the longest cantilever spans in the world - a bold steel answer to the Tay disaster, still carrying trains today.
